name: Constant-Rate Backend Degradation and Recovery
description: Five heterogeneous backends receive 80 requests/s for 160 seconds. Backend A slows from 20ms to 300ms at 40 seconds and returns to 20ms at 100 seconds. Jitter and capacities stay constant.

evaluation.primary_hypothesis: Backend A's temporary capacity reduction changes routing and queueing under fixed offered load; policies may differ in how quickly traffic shifts and returns.

policy_expectations.round_robin: Cyclic routing keeps Backend A's assignment share close to one fifth.
policy_expectations.least_requests: Outstanding work diverts selections away from a queueing backend.
policy_expectations.p2c: A busy Backend A is less likely to win a sampled comparison.
policy_expectations.p2c_peak_ewma: Recent response latency and outstanding work affect Backend A's assignment share.
policy_expectations.ucb1: Observations from both conditions contribute to the running mean.
policy_expectations.sliding_window_ucb: Earlier observations expire as new rewards complete.
policy_expectations.discounted_ucb: Earlier observations progressively lose weight as new rewards complete.
